title: Stale policy cache causes per-org rate limits to be ignored after policy rollout
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Symptom: After a policy rollout that tightens per-org token buckets, a subset of gateways continued to accept requests at the old higher limits for several minutes. This resulted in quota overshoot for affected orgs and unexpected billing spikes for two customers. The problem appears intermittent and correlated with policy updates that happen while the in-memory policy cache is populated across multiple regional frontends. Impact: high (customer billing inaccuracies + potential SLA violations). Scope: observed in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 frontends during a canary-style rollout. Hypothesis: stale local cache entries + non-atomic policy version handshake between control plane and gateways causes enforcement engines to use mixed policy versions; in some cases enforcement is skipped when policy version mismatches are detected but not handled properly. Immediate mitigation: apply emergency server-side kill-switch to force gateways to reload policy from central store on update and temporarily lower global burst allowance to prevent further overshoot.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create an org with a narrow per-org rate limit (e.g., 60 req/min).
2) Start a client generating sustained requests at 100 req/min through a single API key routed to a multi-AZ gateway.
3) Trigger a policy change that reduces the per-org limit to 30 req/min via the control plane API and perform a staged rollout to all regions.
4) Observe some gateways continuing to allow ~100 req/min for 2-8 minutes before enforcement drops to the new limit. Check enforcement logs and policy_version headers.
5) Reproduce by toggling the rollout speed and restarting a subset of gateway instances to emulate partial cache invalidation.
6) Capture metrics: per-org token debit logs, policy_version applied, gateway reload events, and any policy-fetch errors.
investigation_notes: Observed policy_version header mismatch in enforcement traces: requests marked as v42 but enforcement used v41 counters.
Redis-backed central policy store shows update at 2026-03-05T14:02:12Z; several gateways report no policy_fetch event until 14:03:05Z.
Frontend local cache has TTL of 120s; during fast rollouts TTL allowed stale policies to be used until expiry rather than proactively invalidating.
Race: control plane sends "policy_updated" webhook; gateway processes event but stale worker threads continue using older in-memory object until GC; we found non-threadsafe mutation path.
Enforcement path: when policy_version mismatch is detected enforcement returns OK and falls back to route-level default (which in affected orgs was higher), leading to bypass.
Related anomaly: per-token accounting entries were still written correctly, causing billing showing higher usage while enforcement should have limited it.
Relevant logs: https://dash.internal.redwood/logs?span=policy-update-20260305 (console link to filtered logs)
Initial hotfix (applied 2026-03-05 14:18Z): forced synchronous policy reload on gateway startup; reduced global burst window to 10 tokens to limit overshoot. Customer refunds pending.
proposed_fix: 1) Fix non-threadsafe mutation in gateway policy cache: make cache updates copy-on-write and publish atomically to worker threads.
2) Implement policy version handshake: enforcement checks request.policy_version header vs cache and triggers synchronous reload if mismatch is detected (fail closed to conservative enforcement).
3) Add immediate invalidation path: control plane will push a signed invalidate message to all regions; gateways must ack or enter degraded mode.
4) Add unit and integration tests simulating concurrent policy updates and enforcement under heavy load.
5) Post-deploy: add a migration that proactively reloads policy on gateway upgrade and on any change to per-org limits.
6) Follow-up: review TTL heuristics and make them adaptive based on rollout velocity and number of affected orgs.
testing_plan: - Unit: exercise cache update race via thread-scheduling fakes; assert no stale view observed by enforcement threads.
- Integration: multi-AZ test harness that simulates control plane update broadcast and simultaneous request fanout; verify enforcement converges < 5s.
- Load: replay traffic at 3x normal peak during rollout to ensure no enforcement bypass under load.
- Regression: run existing billing/usage accounting suite to confirm no duplicate or missing tokens are written when enforcement reloads.
- Canary rollout: 5% of gateways for 1 hour then expand to 50% with close monitoring on per-org overshoot metrics.
monitoring_and_rollout: Pre-merge checks: lint + race-detector enabled in gateway build, new unit tests passing.
Canary: deploy to canary region with synthetic tenant generating traffic at target + burst to validate enforcement.
Dashboards to watch: per-org overshoot rate, policy_fetch_latency, policy_version_mismatch_rate, billing anomalies by org.
Alert thresholds: overshoot_rate > 0.5% for more than 2 min triggers rollback; policy_fetch_failure_rate > 1% triggers rollback.
Rollback plan: revert gateway binary and re-enable old cache invalidation behavior if canary shows regressions.
Customer communications: CS has draft explaining detection, mitigation, refund timeline, and preventative steps.
